title: Point mimid at the openmls SemiPrivateMessage wire format, and stop duplicating the frame codec
description:
openmls commit 6665d9b80 on branch mimid-0.9.2 (2026-11-26, local, not
pushed) adds the mls_semiprivate_message wire format behind feature
`semiprivate-message-draft`: the WireFormat variant 0x0011, the
MlsMessageBodyIn/Out bodies, and an `openmls::semiprivate_message`
module with the frame types. 4 new tests, openmls's own 379 still pass,
and the crate builds with the feature off, on, and alongside
targeted-messages-draft.

## Blocked on a push

mimid's [patch.crates-io] pins a git rev, so the commit has to be on
github.com/MarkAtwood/openmls before Cargo.toml can move to it. Pushing
needs Mark's OK (AGENTS.md).

Nothing in mimid uses it yet, so the pin and the feature move together
with the sender-side work in bead mimid-1wgh.4.79.3 rather than on their
own.

## The duplication to resolve, deliberately not now

mimi-mls has its own `wire::SemiPrivateMessage` with its own codec, and
openmls now has one too. Two codecs for one wire structure is a real
divergence risk: a change to either could pass its own tests while the
two disagree.

mimi-mls's `wire` module exists to wrap openmls types -- `HPKECiphertext`
is already an opaque newtype over `openmls::prelude::HpkeCiphertext` with
canonical re-encoding -- so the resolution is for
`wire::SemiPrivateMessage` to wrap openmls's once the pin moves.

Until then, the cheap guard is a test that decodes the SAME hand-encoded
fixture with both codecs and asserts the fields and the re-encoded bytes
match. That catches divergence the moment it appears and costs one test.
Write that first; the wrapping refactor can follow.

## Not in this commit, and why

The §3.1 encryption and decryption stay out of openmls for now. They
need the sender's handshake ratchet, which is `pub(crate)` beside
PrivateMessage, and exposing secret-tree key material publicly is an API
change openmls maintainers would be right to push back on. mimid does
the crypto itself in mimi-mls, where it already has the per-message
keys.

An upstream PR for this needs its own branch off upstream/main, as
export-commitin-and-authdata was: mimid-0.9.2 is on the v0.9 line and
diverges from main.
design:
Mark 2026-11-26: use the openmls work, not a second copy.

## What is duplicated

- mimi-mls `wire::SemiPrivateMessage`: codec plus the crypto
  (unseal_keys, framed_content_tbs, open_as_external_receiver).
- openmls `semiprivate_message::SemiPrivateMessage` (commit 6665d9b80,
  branch mimid-0.9.2, local): the frame and its codec only.

Two codecs for one wire structure. mimi-mls `wire` exists to wrap
openmls types -- HPKECiphertext already wraps openmls HpkeCiphertext --
so wire::SemiPrivateMessage wraps openmls's, keeps its own crypto
methods, and the public API mimid calls does not change.

## Why this is blocked, and what else it blocks

mimid's [patch.crates-io] pins openmls by git rev
(64f9eab2fad09ed2ec42d0facab183082b6b458c), which predates 6665d9b80.
A git-rev pin cannot name a local commit, so 6665d9b80 has to be on
github.com/MarkAtwood/openmls first. Pushing needs Mark's OK.

The push is on the critical path for everything left in bead
mimid-1wgh.4.79.3, not just this cleanup:

- mimi-mls `MLSMessage` decodes through openmls `MlsMessageIn`
  (wire/rfc9420.rs decode_canonical). openmls at the pinned rev has no
  0x0011 variant, so it refuses the discriminant.
- So mimi-mls `wire::WireFormat` cannot gain MlsSemiPrivateMessage.
- So mimi_protocol `handshake_content_type` (update.rs:27) cannot accept
  one, which is what decision mimid-1wgh.4.12 recorded: "protocol-07
  §5.3 also allows a SemiPrivateMessage, which MLSMessage cannot decode,
  so it never reaches this check".
- So the hub cannot route a handshake to Hub::read_semiprivate, which is
  why nothing outside tests calls it.

## Order once pushed

1. Cargo.toml: rev to 6665d9b80, add feature semiprivate-message-draft.
2. A test decoding ONE hand-encoded fixture with both codecs, asserting
   the fields and the re-encoded bytes match. Write this before the
   wrapper: it is what catches divergence, and after the wrapper there
   is only one codec to test.
3. wire::SemiPrivateMessage wraps openmls's; its crypto methods stay.
4. wire::WireFormat gains MlsSemiPrivateMessage; MLSMessage decodes it.
5. handshake_content_type accepts it; update decision mimid-1wgh.4.12,
   whose premise stops being true.
6. The hub routes a semiprivate handshake to read_semiprivate.

## Done 2026-11-26, in a different form than planned

Steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 as written. Step 3 took the lower-churn form: rather
than a newtype over openmls's frame, wire::SemiPrivateMessage keeps its
fields and delegates Size, Serialize and Deserialize to openmls's type
through to_openmls and from_openmls. A newtype meant about 90 call sites
(40 external field uses, 50 internal) and the risk being removed was two
CODECS, not two field sets.

mimid's two stricter checks moved into from_openmls: an application
content_type is refused while decoding, where openmls accepts any
ContentType and refuses it in validate, and MAX_EXTERNAL_RECEIVERS is
mimid's invented cap. So mimid's parse stays stricter than openmls's
while sharing its codec, and wire_semiprivate_cross_codec records that
difference rather than leaving it to be discovered.

Evidence the projection is faithful: all 27 pre-existing semiprivate
tests, the hand-encoded fixtures and the real-HPKE end-to-end among
them, pass against openmls's codec unchanged.

Also done here, after openmls gained the accessors: ContentSpans no
longer tracks a signature offset. SemiPrivateMessageContent::signature
reads it from FramedContentAuthData, and the test that checked the old
arithmetic now checks that accessor against the raw wire bytes instead.
ContentSpans keeps only content, which must stay a span because the
TBS hash covers bytes a re-encoded ProposalIn need not reproduce.

Step 6 is not here. It is bead mimid-1wgh.4.79.13: the hub cannot apply
a semiprivate handshake, because openmls cannot process one.
